title: Open ranges on a toy graph
starter:
type node =
  | Range of string * int      (* a named loop counter and its bound *)
  | Const of int
  | Add of node * node
  | Store of node * node        (* offset, value *)
  | End of node * node          (* effect, range: closes that range *)

(* The names of the ranges [n] depends on that no End has closed, sorted, no duplicates. *)
let rec opens (n : node) : string list =
  []

samples.expr: let i = Range ("i", 4) in opens (Add (i, Const 1))
samples.label: let i = Range ("i", 4) in opens (Add (i, Const 1))

hints: A Range is open in itself; a Const has nothing open. Everything else takes the union of its children.
End (e, r) is the one exception: the opens of e, minus r's name.
Keep the result sorted and deduplicated, for example with `List.sort_uniq compare` on the combined lists.

answer.code:
type node =
  | Range of string * int
  | Const of int
  | Add of node * node
  | Store of node * node
  | End of node * node

let rec opens (n : node) : string list =
  match n with
  | Range (s, _) -> [s]
  | Const _ -> []
  | Add (a, b) | Store (a, b) -> List.sort_uniq compare (opens a @ opens b)
  | End (e, r) ->
    let gone = (match r with Range (s, _) -> s | _ -> "") in
    List.filter (fun x -> x <> gone) (opens e)
answer.explain: Open ranges are a union over sources, with Range adding its own name and End removing the range it closes. `List.sort_uniq compare` keeps the result canonical. The real compiler memoizes this per node, because shared subgraphs would otherwise be walked many times.
